Whenever the players want their heroes to do something that is uncertain with a reasonable possibility of failure, then the director has a case to prompt the players for a check.

Since the heroes in the system do not have a prescribed list of skills, the players must leverage their heroes' attributes and traits and have a conversation with the director regarding what to use.

The director will usually be the one to prompt what attributes to use for a check

Short Rest

During short rest scenes, for every 2 PCs in the party one of them can perform an activity.

You should rotate among yourselves and avoid consecutive repeats.

Long Rest

We call the times when the heroes retire for the day at a safe location (such as a settlement or at camp) long rests. In these locations the heroes are able to restock their supplies, unwind and fully prepare for their next day.

During long rest scenes, each PC fully recovers their hit points, mind points, inventory points and clears all their tension points.

When the heroes are in settlement or exploring a location they may want to do certain actions whose resolution should be simple and painless.

These will be covered in this section.

Gathering Information

When the players want to spend time gaining information about people, places or things they can make an INS WLP check.

We define a Journey in the system as the activity performed when the party travels from their current location to a distant one over the course of one day or more.

When there is risk involved, we call that a journey and make use of the rules in this section. Each journey will begin with a travel check.

Travel Check

Once the heroes have decided on a destination and have confirmed they are setting out, the party will make a travel check. A player can volunteer one of their heroes to make the check using the dice listed below.

Location

Danger Level

Travel Check

Settlements

Low

D4

Road

Moderate

D6

Wilderness

High

D8

Remote Locale

Severe

D10

Hazardous Locale

Extreme

D12

Outer Space

D20

  • On a result of 6 or higher, the party encounters a danger.

  • On a result of 1, the party makes a discovery.

After the check and its resulting event is resolved, the party will enter a long rest scene at their Camp. Here the heroes can unwind, work on their downtime projects and deepen their relationships.

Most journeys can be resolved with a single travel check. Refrain from making more than that unless it's a very long journey lest you bog down your session.

Dangers

Hazard

The party can encounter a natural hazard, which will be taxing to traverse.

Ambush

The party can be beset upon by hostile creatures.

Loss

The party loses an important item or a piece of equipment. Let the players volunteer it.

Villain

The party can encounter a villain or one of their associates.

Discoveries

One of the most positive outcomes of a travel check is that of a discovery, which can be one of the following.

Location

An entrance to an abandoned keep. A waterfall with a hidden entrance behind it. All of these are locations where exciting developments can occur and where danger lurks. A chance for the heroes to test themselves and learn more about the world.

Guests

There are many individuals of an adventurous streak who make a living in the world. When you encounter one of them and yours goals align perhaps they can join your party for a time. Maybe they need help. Maybe you are the ones in need of help. (See the rules for Guests).

Merchant

It is not uncommon for enterprising merchants to travel the lands, especially while making use of roads or when traveling to settlements. In such encounters perhaps such merchants can offer the party some rare items or consumables?

Treasure

Heroes may uncover treasure by chance while traveling through an abandoned area. Such treasure can be a rare ingredient or material, a piece of equipment or perhaps a plot-relevant item that leads to heroes gathering more information.

Vista

During travel one of the possible discoveries is that of a vista. A breathtaking locale or solemn monument. In short, they are memorable places of your party's journey.

When encountering one, the players are incentivized to take the lead in describing it and how it fits with the setting.

If one of the players decides to contribute art for it, they get bonus points! You will want to save it in your album.

A ritual is an activity performed whenever a hero with a magical aptitude wants to perform a magical feat outside of a battle.

If a spiritist wants to free a tormented ghost or if an elementalist wants to pacify rampant elementals in a location, this is the activity they would perform in the system.

They are meant to be straightforward procedures which parameters are a conversation between the ritual caster and the director.

First the player states if they could perhaps do X using a ritual in order to achieve an outcome they desire. They make an argument in good faith based on their character's traits and how they could reasonably be capable.

The director then deliberates on whether a ritual would suitable to the situation If so, they then coordinate with the player to set the Potency and the Area of the ritual, the factors which determine its difficulty and cost in mind points.

Parameters

Traits

The character who wishes to perform the ritual must have traits that would be relevant to it. For example a ritual where the character wants to help a spirit move on would require the Light trait that spiritists get. Perhaps Dark if the player in question makes a compelling argument for it.

Potency

The Potency affects the difficulty and base cost of the ritual. The more difficult something is to achieve the higher the potency required of the ritual will be.

Cost

Difficulty

Easy

30

7

10

50

13

Impossible

50

Area

The Area affects the scope of the ritual. Whether limited to a single object or a whole room and bigger besides.

Factor

Example

Entity

1

A single person or object.

Small

Large

Huge

Outcome

A ritual can have four distinct outcomes based on the result of the check.

Outcome

Critical

They get what they hoped for and more besides.

Success

They get what they want.

Partial

They mostly get what they want but there are minor complications.

Fumble

Something went terribly wrong and there are major complications.

Based on the outcome, the director will decide what happens.

When it comes to coming up with a complication on the spot it can be a good idea to bring the players into coming up with an interesting one. Having a conversation about it can help.

As always, complications that arise from rituals must be interesting and add to the narrative.

In this chapter will cover the systems and mechanics that the system provides for the exploration phase of your episodes, where the heroes move about advancing the narrative.

They will be meeting people, traveling the world, learning new facts and potentially getting themselves into danger which can lead to battles.

A montage is a scene or a set of scenes where the party is trying to achieve something that is fairly complicated, involving more than one location and various adversaries and dangers.

These represent the challenges that the heroes face outside of battles.

The director makes the call of when to escalate something from a simple group check onto a montage and begin the procedure which involves a conversation with the players for setting up the stakes.

It is structured as follows:

  • Goal: The director spells out explicitly what the end goal for the montage is. For example it could be "infiltrating the imperial prison" or "making it to the last cabin in the train".

  • Adversities: The director describes what complications the heroes will face such as people, things or events. This provides the players with guidance on what problems their heroes should be solving and how. Each of these need to be dealt with by the heroes in one manner or another lest they create a complication for the party at the resolution.

  • Complications: Each of the described adversities has a matching complications that will occur if they are not resolved. These complications are problems that occur at the resolution of the montage. If that leads to a battle, it makes the starting battle conditions unfavorable to the party.

  • Approach: In the montage, each player makes a single attribute check by the first deciding on their PC will be doing during the montage. Each approach has a distinct set of attributes to be used and offer the party with the option to either overcome one of the complications or to gain advantages in the next battle scene.

Complications

The number of complications depends on the difficulty level of the montage.

Easy

1/2 Party Size

Normal

Party Size

Hard

Party Size + 2

Impossible

Party Size + 4

The players should be made aware of each of the adversities and matching complications at the onset of the montage.

It is expected for players in the more difficult montages to make a strategic decision on which adversities they want to deal with and which they can't.

Approaches

After the players select an approach they must describe how their hero will contribute in the montage. If they want to directly address an adversity they must specifically describe how their heroes will do so, prompting the corresponding attribute check specific to the approach.

The outcomes for the check are as follows.

Critical Success

They resolve the adversity and can choose one advantage unique to the approach.

Success

They can resolve the adversity or choose one advantage unique to the approach.

Partial

They resolve the adversity but suffer Stress as a result.

Fumble

They fail to deal with the adversity.

When choosing advantages for their approaches, the players can decide immediately or do so at the start of the scene following the end of the montage, after the director has set the stage. If it led to a battle this must happen before the first round of battle.

Once all players have resolved their approaches, the director describes the outcome of the montage and to what fictional state it has led the story to.

This type of Check performed during battle and is used when a character performs various actions such as attacks, skills and spells. Its result determines how potent the action was, in various tiers.

Any actions that lead to this check cannot miss and achieve nothing. Their consequences (such as taking damage) can only be avoided or diminished through the use of specific defensive actions.

Depending on the result of the check, the potency of the action varies.

Failure

Reduced

Usually minimal damage with no extra effects.

Success

Standard

Average damage with default effects.

Critical

Powerful

Same as standard, provides an opportunity.

Examples

Meravel attacks a Wolf which has 8 DEF.

13

Success

The wolf suffers the sword’s (base bonus + high roll) in physical damage.

7

Failure

The wolf suffers (base bonus * 0.5) in physical damage.

16

Critical Success

The wolf suffers (base bonus + high roll) and the character gets an opportunity. CB is a valid opportunity option.
This type of Check is performed when two characters oppose each other in an action.
